content.title: About
content.content: Nougat with nuts is a confection made from whipped egg whites, sugar, honey, and roasted nuts (commonly walnuts, hazelnuts or almonds). It has a soft, slightly chewy texture and a flavor that blends sweet caramel notes with the aroma of toasted nuts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nougat has ancient roots: its ancestors were prepared in ancient Rome and Persia.
Traditionally, nuts are toasted to a golden hue before being folded into the nougat to release their flavor.
Different countries use different nuts: Italy often uses almonds, France prefers hazelnuts.
Nougat is frequently used as a filling for cakes, chocolates and ice cream.
Legend says the original nougat was created in the 13th century in the Arab town of Nuga.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Sugar and honey provide quick‑acting glucose, delivering an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Healthy fats from nuts
items.content: Nuts contain monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats that support heart health.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Nuts are rich in vitamin E, magnesium and selenium, which have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Protein
items.content: The nuts add plant‑based protein, useful for tissue repair and satiety.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Nuts contribute fiber that aids normal digestion.

items.title: Tree‑nut allergy
items.content: Nougat with nuts can trigger severe allergic reactions in people sensitive to nuts.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The large amount of sugar makes nougat calorie‑dense and may contribute to tooth decay if consumed frequently.

items.title: Honey content
items.content: Children under one year should not consume honey, so this confection is unsuitable for infants.

items.title: Added additives
items.content: Some manufacturers add artificial flavors or preservatives, which some consumers may wish to avoid.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Nougat with nuts can be enjoyed on its own, crumbled over pastries, used as a cake filling, or mixed into yogurt and ice cream. For a smoother texture, nuts can be finely chopped before incorporation.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep nougat in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, store it in the refrigerator to prevent sugar crystallisation. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odors, or discoloration.
